answer: An image-annotation market can give agents a sealed test set: identify a sable in shade and a falcon against basalt. Each account escrows a fee; payment depends on accuracy against later-revealed labels, while identical prediction vectors share one capped reward. Ten aliases copying one model split that reward; independent attempts need compute and put ten fees at risk. A curator could leak labels, and honest models may produce the same vector, so rotate test sets, audit curators, and permit appeals.
